answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.2.2026) Any company operating in the EU, including branches of Belarusian companies, must comply with EU restrictive measures (sanctions). Trade sanctions on Belarus mirror those applicable to Russia. From the outset, EU sanctions have been carefully targeted to restrict Russia’s capacity to wage war while minimising effects on EU citizens and companies.

Overall, the data confirms the Commission's longstanding principle: sanctions are crafted to hurt those responsible of the behaviours that such tools are intended to tackle. The Commission continuously monitors the situation and proposes adjustments to the measures where necessary with a view to strengthening their implementation and preventing their circumvention.
It is for the Council to decide unanimously on the amendment and adoption of sanctions in line with EU law.
